summary.intent: Close the caliper-docgen v1 alpha gap: record a baseline, ship schema v4 (readonly, index signatures, RefObject), root-cause the shadcn/antd recall gap, add detection by shape, and harden on-demand TS 7.1. Later the user asked to plan the follow-up work properly with trails, sessions and workflows.
summary.outcome: Baseline recorded on trail #125; PRs #266 (schema v4), #267 (detection by shape) and #268 (on-demand hardening) were opened ready and signed. The shadcn/antd gap was reframed as mostly collapse/harness pairing, research was run, and a six-trail plan was saved to a plan file with coordinator and worker prompts; no further trails or branches were created.

repo: Collapsed inheritance layers (ADR 0012) store only type name, source, omitted list and total_props, so recall measured on flat props undercounts; shadcn own-props recall is 49.7% default vs 91.1% with --collapse-inherited-props none, antd 86.4% vs 99.3%.
An index signature [key: string]: T converted to an object field named `key` leaked into props-base consumers and produced a spurious `key` prop; consumers of object fields must skip index fields.
Snapshot tests resolve node_modules from the checkout, so a fresh worktree needs `npm install` or snapshots differ from CI.
Entire opens a draft PR on `entire trail link`; fill that PR in with gh pr edit/ready instead of gh pr create.
Weekly harness pairing errors (same-file default aliases, displayName, Object.assign/as barrels) account for ~27 antd misses; fixing pairing lifts antd component recall from 79.7% to ~95.4%.

Profiling with deps loaded showed the new-feature cost came from project_demands sorting (~10ms), module-only demands parsing ~580 extra files (~10ms, 50MiB), and per-read augmentation lookup (~5.5ms), not from members lists or JSON size.

scripts/rdt.mjs stores only the string 'enum' for enum props and the weekly react-docgen run loses 17-21% of files to thrown errors; vanilla react-docgen follows relative imports contrary to docs/measurement.md.

Callisto 0.16.0 is latest; callisto.toml publish-to lacks "github-release" and has no [release] section, so no GitHub Releases are created; release.yml asserts zero artifact slots and lacks release pending/drain recovery jobs.
workflow: The user's environment has a GH shim whose credentials are in sandbox-denied paths; running gh unsandboxed bypassed it without the agent knowing.
Run the sandbox off for git/gh per repo rules but ask before bypassing controls; confirm any shim or wrapper exists before working around sandbox failures.

Per-trail sessions started from the trail body (`entire trail checkout N --worktree`, `entire trail resume N`) with a coordinator session is the recommended structure; cap about three concurrent sessions and profile alone.
Research subagents/workflows with read-only worktrees were effective for root-causing; their results live only in journals, so key facts must be copied into the plan file or trail bodies.
